title: Atrx and Chd8 perturbations move Csf2ra in opposite directions in TH and MB glutamatergic neurons
exact_observed_result: Atrx produced only ten FDR<0.05 rows across 18 tested cell types, but Csf2ra was FDR-repressed in both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. Chd8 induced Csf2ra in those same cell classes with FDR support.
biological_interpretation: The Csf2ra marker is not a generic chromatin-loss response: ATRX and CHD8 have opposite signed effects on the same transcript in the two strongest Csf2ra-responsive neuronal contexts.

support.description: Atrx and Chd8 have opposite Csf2ra direction in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic cells.
Atrx has a sparse thalamic signature with Cyp46a1/Pigk/Pnpla6 down and Begain up; 007 L2/3 IT CTX contributes an isolated Limd2 increase.

caveats: Atrx target RNA itself was not FDR-depleted; all target-row FDR values were 1.0.
The direct literature prior links ATRX and CHD8 to chromatin and neurodevelopment, not specifically to Csf2ra regulation in neurons.

prior_expectation.summary: ATRX is an ATRX:DAXX/H3.3 chromatin remodeler with neurodevelopmental loss phenotypes, while CHD8 is an autism-associated chromatin regulator; the opposite neuronal Csf2ra direction is therefore dataset-specific.

citations.citation: Berube et al., Journal of Clinical Investigation, 2005. PMID:15668733.
